newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cardoso's popularity keeps on growing in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Cardoso's popularity keeps on growing in Brazil.

text.p: The popularity of Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso continues to grow with his personal approval rating now at 70 percent, up from 61 percent in November, a new poll said.

The poll, by the private Brazilian Public Opinion and Statistics Institute (Ibope), found 21 percent of 3,000 people interviewed between February 28 and March 5 disapproved of the way he was running the country. Eight percent had no opinion.
The poll also found that Cardoso's popularity ratings were highest among Brazil's poorest and least educated sectors.
Seventy-three percent of respondents with only first-grade schooling approved of the president, falling to 54 percent among people with a university education.

Region to region, support for Cardoso was highest in Brazil's impoverished Northeast, at 76 percent, while the industrial heartlands of the Southeast gave him 69 percent, falling to 64 percent in the South.
Ibope did not give a margin of error for its poll.
